subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 58-year-old man with refractory cutaneous T-cell lymphoma begins treatment with a histone deacetylase inhibitor. After therapy, tumor cells show increased expression of several genes.
question: Which of the following best explains the increased transcription?

options.text: Increased methylation of CpG islands in the promoters of these genes.
Removal of acetyl groups from histones, tightening DNA coiling.
Increased positive charge on histone lysine residues, strengthening their binding to DNA.
Accumulation of acetylated histones, neutralizing their positive charge and relaxing DNA coiling.
Proteasomal degradation of nucleosomes, removing histones from DNA.

explanation_correct: Histones are positively charged because of lysine and arginine residues and bind negatively charged DNA. Acetylation neutralizes the positive charge, relaxing DNA coiling and increasing transcription; histone deacetylase inhibitors prevent removal of acetyl groups, keeping chromatin open and increasing expression of target genes. Deacetylation, conversely, tightens coiling and decreases transcription.

explanation_incorrect.A: CpG methylation silences genes; this drug inhibits deacetylation, not methylation.
explanation_incorrect.B: Removal of acetyl groups is what the inhibited enzyme would do; blocking deacetylation increases acetylation, which relaxes rather than tightens chromatin.
explanation_incorrect.C: Acetylation neutralizes the positive charge of lysine residues and weakens histone-DNA binding; increased positive charge would tighten chromatin and suppress transcription.
explanation_incorrect.E: Histone deacetylase inhibitors alter histone modification, not proteasomal degradation of nucleosomes.

educationalObjective: Histone acetylation neutralizes the positive charge of lysine residues, relaxing DNA coiling and increasing transcription, whereas deacetylation tightens chromatin and suppresses transcription.
